messages:
Adele (Support): FYI customer reported SSO sign-in errors starting this morning after their regional DST change. They see 401s from our token verification. Error: 'invalid signature'.

Maya (Customer): yep, happened ~07:12 local time. Some users can login intermittently. Most get 401.

Adele (Support): attaching our logs snippet and repro steps.
```
2026-03-17T07:11:58Z verify_token failed: jws: signature verification failed (kid: bXktc2VydmljZS1rZXk=)
2026-03-17T07:12:03Z jwks_cache: served key from cache (age=3598s, ttl=3600s)
2026-03-17T07:12:03Z verify_token: fetch_jwks on kid-miss returned 200 but key not found
```

Adele (Support): repro: curl -> POST /api/auth/callback with token from their SSO-proxy. Sometimes verification passes, sometimes fails.

Kevin (Eng-Security): curious — cache age ~3598s suggests JWKS cached ~1hr TTL and right at expiry. Could be race between cache refresh and concurrent requests. Also DST could have made their proxy re-issue tokens right when keys rotated.

Samir (Eng-Infra): can you paste the JWT header (base64)? need to confirm kid in token vs JWKS.

Maya (Customer): header: `{ "alg":"RS256","typ":"JWT","kid":"bXktc2VydmljZS1rZXk=" }`. Our JWKS endpoint returns keys A and B, but sometimes our proxy uses a newly minted key C (not in cached jwks).

Kevin (Eng-Security): classic KID-miss + stale cache. Our verifier currently: 1) check cache; 2) if kid not found, return 401 and rely on caller to retry. We should instead attempt a refetch of JWKS on kid-miss and then retry verification once.

Samir (Eng-Infra): agree. Also we have an optimization that only refreshes JWKS every TTL (3600s) and suppresses upstream calls during refresh window. If many concurrent requests arrive during refresh, some may still use stale index and then get 401 even though a background refresh is in-flight.

Kevin (Eng-Security): short-term mitigation: add logic to on-kid-miss -> force-refresh JWKS (with a single in-flight fetch dedupe) and re-run verification one time. Also add a small leeway for exp/nbf (e.g., 120s) to cope with clock skew.

Adele (Support): can we ship that as a hotfix? Customer is in production, impacting logins.

Samir (Eng-Infra): I can patch runtime today. Plan: 1) change verifier to attempt fetch-if-kid-miss (dedupe fetches), 2) increase leeway to 120s configurable, 3) log a metric for 'kid_miss_refetch' to monitor. Will deploy to canary and then prod.

Kevin (Eng-Security): also add fallback: if fetch returns new JWKS but still no matching kid, log the token kid in sanitized form and emit an alert to security - could indicate replay or mis-issuing.

Adele (Support): repro steps for on-call to validate after deploy:
- use their SSO-proxy to mint a token with kid C
- call our /api/auth/callback 100x in ~30s window
- observe that token verification succeeds after refetch instead of 401 storm

Samir (Eng-Infra): creating rollout PR now. small patch to verifier:
```go
if !cache.contains(kid) {
  if fetchJWKSOnce(kid) { // deduped single fetch across threads
    tryVerifyAgain()
  } else {
    return 401
  }
}
```

Jon (SRE Bot): Incident created: INC-2026-0423 — SSO token verification intermittent — priority P2. Pager notified for >50% login failure rate.

Kevin (Eng-Security): question: why did DST trigger this? likely coincidence: their key rotation aligned with their wall-clock change and some tokens were minted with new kid while our cache still had old set. Not a clock problem per se, but clock-skew leeway still helpful for exp/nbf tiny mismatches.

Maya (Customer): we also run a caching SSO-proxy in front of our IdP that served a stale JWKS for a bit due to internal caching. We'll reduce their proxy cache TTL too.

Adele (Support): noted. Customer next steps: reduce proxy jwks-cache TTL to 30s and let us know when done.

Samir (Eng-Infra): deployed hotfix to canary 10:20 UTC, canary traffic saw kid_miss_refetch=43 with 100% success on retried verifications. Rolling to prod now.

Kevin (Eng-Security): post-deploy follow-ups:
- add automated test for kid-miss refetch path,
- add docs in auth runbook about 'force-refresh on kid-miss' and expected metrics,
- consider exposing a per-tenant jwks-leeway override for enterprise customers.

Adele (Support): marking customer update: we applied a server-side mitigation (force-refetch) and asked customer to lower proxy cache TTL. They reported logins recovered within ~12min. :white_check_mark:

Maya (Customer): thanks everyone — observers said 0 failures after your change. appreciate the fast turnaround.

Samir (Eng-Infra): closing thread after monitoring window. Will follow up with PR link and changelog entry.

Kevin (Eng-Security): PR: https://git.redwood.ai/r/infra/verify-jwks-refetch/ (will add tests + docs).

Adele (Support): closing on our side. If anything flares up we'll re-open. :slightly_smiling_face:
